messages:
Lena: Quick sync — proposing a lightweight 'micro-sweeper' runbook for accounts with healthscore_v3 between 0.30-0.50, low activity (last_seen > 30d), and no owner change in 7d. Goal: catch edge cases and capture enablement feedback without touching high-ARR or enterprise accounts.
Tom: 👍 what’s the minimal safe flow? dry-run -> nudge -> handoff -> feedback? any automation to avoid noisy churn triggers?
Lena: Exactly. Proposal:
1) dry-run export of 200 sampled accounts (dedupe by canonical_contact_id)
2) enablement pilot: 20 accounts for human outreach
3) capture feedback via a short form + attach notes to account
4) auto-snooze flagged accounts from sweep for 14d
Ravi: Enablement can take 20. What fields should the export include so our notes map back to the healthscore signal?
Ava: I'll produce an export with these columns: account_id, account_name, last_seen, healthscore_v3, owner_id, primary_contact_email, arr_bucket, playbook_disabled_flag, canonical_contact_id. Command I’ll run:
```
python tools/export_micro_sweeper.py --sample 200 --dedupe canonical_contact_id --out s3://redwood-cs/micro_sweeper/2026-03-? .csv
```
Please confirm the sample size and the ARR cutoff we should exclude.
Tom: Keep sample 200 for dry-run. Exclude arr_bucket IN (">250k","enterprise") to avoid risky changes. Also add rule: skip accounts with active onboarding task in the last 30d.
Lena: Good call. Also add a safety net: any account with manual account_flag 'do_not_sweep' must be skipped. We should surface that in the export.
Ravi: For the feedback form, simple fields please: account_id, rep, outcome(dropdown: no_response / bad_fit / needs_onboarding / scheduling_call), recommended_next_step (call/email/ps_eng), was_onboarding_complete (yes/no), free_text. I'll build a small Google form and map responses back to account via account_id.
Tom: Can we auto-create a playbook task when enablement marks "scheduling_call"? Otherwise follow-up slips. Maybe a cheap webhook from the form to playbook-runner.
Lena: Yes — plan: form -> webhook -> playbook-runner creates a task assigned to enablement_owner. I'll add the webhook URL to the form. Template nudge text is in the doc: short intro, ask for availability, link to help center.
Ava: Dry-run export completed locally. Uploading to s3 now.
deploy-bot: sweep-dryrun: export finished — 200 accounts written to s3://redwood-cs/micro_sweeper/dryrun_1719982024.csv :white_check_mark:
Lena: Great — @Ravi I’ll DM the sample link + pilot instructions. I’ll also open a PR in infra/playbooks with the nudge template and the playbook-runner webhook mapping.
Ravi: Got it. We'll start the pilot outreach tomorrow morning and report back with the form entries by EOD+2.
Tom: Quick reminder — dedupe step is critical. If two contacts map to same canonical_contact_id, only surface the most recent activity row. Also please add `playbook_disabled_flag` to the QA checklist; we don't want any account nuked by automation.
Ava: S3 link: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-cs/micro_sweeper/dryrun_1719982024.csv
Lena: Thanks — scheduled a 15m sync to walk through the runbook tomorrow 11:00am PST. @Ravi @Tom please join if you can.
Ravi: 👍 will be there.
Tom: :+1: see you then.
